title: Learning from the Worst: Dynamically Generated Datasets to Improve Online Hate Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets (e.g., swapping identity terms) targeting racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Black people, East Asians, Arabs) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting women and gender minorities (e.g., trans and non-binary people) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting religious groups (e.g., Muslims, Jewish people, Hindus) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting sexual orientations (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting people with disabilities to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting immigrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and specific nationalities (e.g., Polish) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.

Human-and-model-in-the-loop dynamic dataset generation where annotators create adversarial hate speech examples and contrast sets targeting class identities (e.g., working class) to trick a target model, evaluated via model error rates and the HateCheck test suite.
